correctness.rationale: Definitions, signs, multiplication order and full graph conventions are explicit. Pairwise sign compatibility is necessary and sufficient for commutation, yielding a canonical common product. Chamber refinements give the complete maximal-clique classification and prefix-intersection formula. Within-block ordered partitions plus one merge bit per boundary give a genuine bijection for each centralizer. Counting nonempty cut-subset labels yields the tuple formula; Stirling inversion yields clique counts, and singularity analysis gives fixed-arity asymptotics. The embedded independent program checks direct products and formulas through stated finite bounds, not arbitrary sizes.

originality.rationale: The specific accepted contribution is the complete semigroup commuting-graph clique geometry and centralizer distribution, not the numerical ordered-Bell/Stirling tuple formula alone. Commins defines the same monoid and studies its face algebra as a module; Carson et al. study broader action pair structures; Brauner et al. study the distinct free band. OEIS A050352 ALREADY gives an equivalent numerical function for all fixed tuple arities through its generalized m-level rooted-tree formula, so the numerical formula, EGF and asymptotic are explicitly excluded from any independent novelty claim. Nearby indexed results concern other algebraic objects. Global priority in left-regular-band literature remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: A general theorem in the extensive left-regular-band or hyperplane-arrangement literature could imply the structural clique or centralizer statements without matching these search terms.
Only the referenced primary works and relevant sections were materially inspected; this is not an exhaustive historical survey.
The exact numeric tuple formula, its EGF and asymptotic are already covered by OEIS rooted-tree formulas and have no standalone originality.

value.rationale: The type-A face monoid is a canonical geometric left-regular band. Its full commuting-graph centralizer distribution, maximal cliques, exact clique intersection multiplicities, and clique-count transform are natural complete invariants; the proof connects weak-order signs to indecomposable permutations. These structural statements give information not contained in a mere known integer sequence. This is a coherent infinite-family classification, not a chosen tiny finite slice or arbitrary computation.
